summary: Today’s pulse tracks Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say, Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says, and Democrats capture at least 258 House seats in largest sweep since 1992. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are attack, officials, and russian. In the background, Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds and What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
headlines.description: Libya's eastern government says the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia.

headlines.title: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says
headlines.description: John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang ’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy”. The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was put at risk by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.

headlines.title: Democrats capture at least 258 House seats in largest sweep since 1992
headlines.description: Milestone reached Sunday, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Virginia Foxx in North Carolina House Democrats have secured their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in a midterm election sweep unseen since 1992 that creates not only vast opportunities to govern but also intense pressure to deliver on campaign promises and priorities. Democrats have gained 44 House seats so far, four more than the 40 they picked up in Donald Trump’s first midterm in 2018.

headlines.title: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds
headlines.description: Transparency International says Queensland’s David Crisafulli was ‘by far the most frequently accessed’ state leader, with 13 meetings Analysis by Transparency International Australia argues these meetings, when combined with political donations, demonstrate “unfettered access” to decision-makers that creates an “uneven playing field”.

headlines.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
headlines.description: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has formally come to an end after countries failed to agree a deal.

headlines.title: Russian ship hit in Benghazi by suspected Ukrainian drone attack, say Libyan officials
headlines.description: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A suspected Ukrainian drone attack caused an explosion on a Russian warship docked at the naval base in the Libyan port city of Benghazi, Libyan officials have said. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy warship, and ignited a fire at the naval base, they said. Several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, the officials told the Associated Press.

headlinePool.title: NHS savings drive leaves hospitals in England facing ‘unpalatable’ cuts
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Thirty-one trusts issue stark warning that cost-cutting demands threaten their ability to function normally Dozens of hospitals are so short of money they may not be able to continue caring for patients and are being forced to make “unpalatable” cuts to services and staff, the Guardian can reveal. Thirty-one health service trusts in England have issued stark warnings that NHS demands for them to make huge budget savings this year threaten their ability to function normally. All have declared that as a threat in the register of risks they have to maintain and publish.

headlinePool.title: US Army to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa despite court order
headlinePool.description: The Army says "swift action" is necessary to protect its personnel and nearby communities around its ammunition plant in Iowa.

headlinePool.title: Hakeem Jeffries willing to cross political aisle to work on Democrats’ agenda
headlinePool.description: Incoming House speaker says party focused on affordability and fixing ‘broken’ healthcare and immigration systems The incoming US House speaker, Hakeem Jeffries , has said he and his fellow Democrats are focused on affordability, expanding healthcare and fixing the “broken” immigration system in the country – and willing to cross the political aisle to do so. Jeffries laid out that agenda in an interview on Sunday with CBS News’s Face the Nation, less than three weeks after Democrats seized control of Congress during the 3 November midterms for the latter half of Donald Trump’s second presidency.

headlinePool.title: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
headlinePool.description: The talks fail to make a breakthrough on tackling climate change after a row about mentioning fossil fuels.

headlinePool.title: 'Danger seems greater all the time': Ukrainians search for missing after Russian strikes
headlinePool.description: The BBC's Sarah Rainsford reports from the scene of a collapsed residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region.

headlinePool.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
headlinePool.description: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge says it took six weeks for him using the AI tool to solve 19th-century Riemann hypothesis A mathematician at Anthropic has said that the San Francisco -based artificial intelligence (AI) company’s software has helped crack one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics – and experts say the claim checks out. Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks. This story was edited on 22 November 2026 to account for updated information: the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative statement claiming to verify the solution was added, and a quote from a prior story from a mathematician was removed, as updates to the news evolved

headlinePool.title: Russell Brand’s wife vows to abide by prison rules after video controversy
headlinePool.description: Laura Gallacher says in new video on YouTube she will continue Sunday Service series she started with Brand Laura Gallacher, Russell Brand’s wife, has promised to “absolutely honour” rules set by the prison where her convicted sex offender husband is being held, in another YouTube video published on Sunday. This week Andy Burnham called on Google to take down a video uploaded to Brand’s YouTube channel last Sunday that contained a statement from the disgraced comedian in prison, where he is serving a 10-and-a-half-year sentence for rape and sexual assaults.

headlinePool.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
headlinePool.description: In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked.

headlinePool.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
headlinePool.description: South Africa is working to overcome a children's literacy crisis. In one Johannesburg township, a reading club is instilling a love of books in kids — and inspiring them to become authors.
